core_obligations: notes that C -> Ind C preserves finite colimits (prop:Ind-colim) and limits (prop:Ind-lim), so it takes the zero object to the zero object and Ind C has finite limits and colimits

shows the canonical morphism delta: Y sqcup Y -> Y x Y of eqn:coprod-prod-delta is always an isomorphism by reducing to X, Y in Obj(C) via the index-wise construction of products and coproducts of ind-objects, and defines f + g via X -> X x X -> Y x Y -> Y sqcup Y -> Y following prop:additive-cat-addition

tells the reader to check the operations reduce to the same addition on Hom_C under Hom(X, Y) = lim_i colim_j Hom_C(X_i, Y_j), making Ind C an Ab-category and an additive category with C -> Ind C additive

using prop:ind-object-morphism (ii) writes f = colim f_i and, with kernels and cokernels in an additive category as in prop:Im-Coim-additive plus Ker(f) = colim Ker(f_i), reduces Coim(f) = Im(f) to Coim(f_i) = Im(f_i) in C, concluding Ind C is abelian; exactness of C -> Ind C and the Pro C statement follow by duality (prop:abelian-cat-duality, Pro C = Ind(C^op)^op)

compared.title: For a flat ring map and a finite ideal the gluing category is abelian and the canonical functor is exact and commutes with colimits
compared.statement:
\label{lemma-exact}
Assume $\varphi : R \to S$ is a flat ring map and let
$I = (f_1, \ldots, f_t) \subset R$ be an ideal.
Then $\text{Glue}(R \to S, f_1, \ldots, f_t)$ is an abelian category, and
the functor $\text{Can}$ is exact and commutes with arbitrary colimits.
